Unpacking day: A different team of two delivered our items - they were very friendly and showed up early. Immediately after the unpacking, I called Lee moving to let them know that our carpet was slightly damaged during the unpacking. I received an email the next day that it would be covered with information on how to process a claim. I decided to check the items in all of the boxes before submitting a claim about a week later. It's during these days that I noticed a nice puncture hole in the top of an armoire as well as a broken candleholder. I took pictures and submitted one claim for all three issues. I reached out to my assigned claims agent to ask the status. She responded via email that I would receive a check for the armoire and candleholder ONLY. I was told to contact Lee moving regarding the damaged carpet. I spoke with the manager on 2 occasions. He stated that he would kindly call me back after he had time to research my inquiry/claim. I received an email that they do not clean carpet - he never called me back. NOTE: The claim was not for the carpet to be cleaned.... My multiple calls to Lee moving has gone ignored. We spent $7k with this company and are being mistreated after trusting our personal items to them for safe transport and delivery. I subsequently filed a complaint with the BBB of Greater New Orleans. The company responded that protection was placed on floors (it was not) and that a final walk through was done (it was not). text: I decided to try this place with a couple of girlfriends on a Tuesday night, not expecting too much of a crowd because of how new Not Your Average Joe's is. I was completely mistaken--the place was packed with Main Liners getting their drink on. Clips from classic movies were playing on a big screen and there was a bar both upstairs and downstairs (bathrooms are upstairs). Not Your Average Joe's has an industrial-chic vibe going on, which lends itself well to the open space. After waiting about twenty minutes, the hostess led us to a high-top near the bar and we got there in time to catch the end of happy hour--cheap select drafts, $5 wine, $2 sliders, and $4 nachos. Our sever walked up soon after and got our drinks in. Overall she was very friendly and the bar has cool tech for ordering/paying, but she was very busy the entire time because of how many people were there. It took us half of our meal to get water. Complimentary bread (delicious focaccia baked in house) and olive oil (mixed with cheese--amazing!!) arrived soon after our drinks and we gorged ourselves on the dip. I went with a pepper jack burger, medium rare, which came with fries (~$11). The burger was dry, but the fries were good and they were even better after I dipped them in the olive oil (extra was brought to us because we gulped down the first plate immediately). My friend needs a gluten-free diet, and she was overjoyed to see that about 3/4 of the menu was available as a gluten-free meal--and this included the complimentary bread baskets. Kudos! Not your average place indeed. I love you, "hot and trending" page on Yelp.

text: It's time to update my review. I can't believe it's been three years. And this place has done nothing but get better with age. But it's still a Puerto Rican restaurant, so it retains a certain charm that your typical chain restaurant can't touch. And the food.... I have to make the disclaimer that I'm Puerto Rican. So when it comes to Puerto Rican food, I'm an expert. I know good Puerto Rican food. And and I know bad and mediocre food. I can unequivocally state this is freaking outstanding Puerto Rican food. In Tampa it just doesn't get any better than this. The taste remains home made. Maintaining that taste in a commercial venture is hard. If you want to taste authentic Puerto Rican food, look no further. Ask for "morcilla". It's blood sausage. Don't Google it. You don't want to know what's in it or how it's made. Trust me. But if you like sausage, you will love this. Just bit into in and don't think too much about it. Ask for "alcapurrias". It's Puerto Rican fried appetizers that are amazingly delicious. They make them in house. It's the real deal. And, of course, there's the mofongo. It's the house specialty. I don't remember having it better even in Puerto Rico. Bring a big empty stomach. You're gonna need it. I eat out all over Tampa Bay and enjoy all sorts of food. I prefer genuine ethnic foods as they tend to be more flavorful and interesting. But I have a soft spot for Puerto Rican food, and I'm glad there is one place in Tampa where I can get the authentic experience without having to go back to the island. Come and enjoy this place. It's as good as it gets.

text: PROS: I can see. CONS: Process slows down once you pay. Be prepared for high-pressure tactics asking you to leave a positive review. I've been thinking about LASIK surgery for 20 years, yes 2-0. Fear of all things eyeball kept me from taking the plunge, but I finally felt fed-up with my contacts. I narrowed down the surgery to Dr. Loden & Dr. Wang. I think they are both fine choices. THE CONSULTATION: I started with the seminar (25% off), which you will need because apparently for the price of LASIK you could buy a used car. The consultation takes 2.5 hours. During that time, they numb your eyes, poke, prod them, & torture them with various lights & apparatuses. They were understanding about the fact that the process sucks & to their credit, I was never sitting around waiting. They then connect you with a patient coordinator who hands you the price tag & suggests which way to go before you are passed to Dr. Wang. He will look over your test results, look at your eyeballs, & tell you everything you've already read on his website but in a soft-spoken manner. THE POST-CONSULTATION PHASE: For some reason, I started panicking after the consultation. Dr. Wang had mentioned that most of his patients get plugs that will dissolve. According to the internet :), plugs should be used as a last resort. Then I found an article about a whistle-blower doctor who blew the lid on a LASIK center for up-charging customers for plugs in the name of profit. To be blunt, this made me lose a lot of trust & I felt sick to my stomach and nervous. I ended up emailing my concerns to Dr. Wang's office, & he called me that night. During our call, I voiced my concerns about the plugs & also other things that I had started to freak out about. After reading on the internet (don't do that) I also started panicking about flap LASIK vs PRK non-flap surgery. And I really wanted PRK. I was able to talk to Dr. Wang about both concerns. The fact that he personally called me & had zero ego about my concerns meant a lot. He explained that plugs are preventative & as so many people have dry eye after surgery, they're worth it. He said I could choose the surgery I wanted (PRK or LASIK), & to let them know what I wanted the day of. THE SURGERY: The day of the surgery I was scheduled to come in at 10:30, I didn't leave until 2:30 = long day. I arrived, they got me in, I told them I wanted PRK, they talked me out of it :). I ended up getting LASIK. They confirmed my prescription & asked me to finalize my payment. I did. Then things slowed down. Ironically or because they had my money? I will never know. But my husband & I did have a good laugh about it. We waited and waited and when they called me again, it was time. They had given me a Valium in advance, it didn't do a damn thing. I told them so, they told me I'd be fine. Did it hurt? No. Was it uncomfortable? At times, it was. A Valium that worked would have been welcome. The clamping of the eye isn't pleasant, & then they do this suction thing which makes everything go black. I'm not going to lie, I flat-out panicked. I wasn't calm, but tried to use yogic breathing, & I managed to stay still enough that it was over before I knew it. I had a teddy bear & a husband. I recommend bringing both if you can as they brought me a lot of comfort. When the surgery was over, I was in complete shock, & I was shaking from hyperventilating during my panic attack. Even though I expressed that I was dizzy, they tried to hurry me off the bed. They moved me to another chair to insert plugs. Before I had even left the operating room, they had another patient in the bed prepping for her procedure. I wasn't into this part at all. Seems like an assembly line. FOLLOW-UP That night there was slight discomfort for a couple of hours.You have to keep your eyes closed for the day. Day two I could see pretty well & I had my follow-up appointment with Dr. Wang, which was a joke. He's so sweet, but the whole visit consisted of waiting for him, a quick look at my eyes, & then a marketing recruitment. "Post this pic on Facebook, write a review here & write one here." Not going to lie, this freaks me out! I want honest reviews, not forced reviews written by half-blind recovering LASIK patients that feel obligated because they were put on a time crunch to write a review before leaving the office. 6 MONTHS LATER: My eyes took forever to heal. They were dry & I feared they would be like that forever. It wasn't until month 3 that I noticed my life might not consist of eye drops every hour. But, they didn't actually heal for 6 months! My advice to others is to remember that you may wake up & be fine the next day, but it may take 3-6 months. Be prepared for that, don't get discouraged if this happens to you. Tips: Take fish oil pills, get a humidifier, & get the surgery done in the summer. They didn't tell me until AFTER my surgery that those that have surgery in the winter usually suffer dry eye more.

text: My initial reaction was to say that I love this place, but after two pretty big let downs I'm giving them a one. I love that they offer a free trial day to see how things go. However, the main reason I sent her was for boarding. The first time I picked her up from a 5 day trip and she had diarrhea all over my car. This was so out of character for her so I knew she was really sick. It bothered me a little that no one said anything to me when I picked her up. I of course called when I got home to see if she had been sick earlier and they said that she did great (same thing they said when I picked her up). They did suddenly remember that she hadn't been eating so they put some wet food in with her dry food (without calling me to check first) to try to get her to eat. They were very apologetic, and said that if she wasn't better by the morning I could take her back and they could give me some meds for her. She was sick all through the night and the next morning, and I wasn't comfortable bringing her someplace for medicine that wasn't her vet so I brought her to the vet just to be safe. Although the folks at P&C were very kind and apologetic, it didn't help clean my car or pay for my vet bill. Granted, she does have a sensitive stomach and I should have mentioned that when I dropped her off so I brushed it off and decided to give it another try. After all, we're all human and we all make mistakes. The second time I was on my way to pick her up from a week long trip when they called me to let me know that my dog was resting because she was limping. I asked what happened, and they said sometimes young dogs don't know their limits and they play too hard so they just gave her some time to rest. Everything was fine when I picked her up and I didn't think much of it until I got her home. That was when I noticed that she had two huge cuts on her hind leg. It would have been no big deal if they simply told me she had gotten into a fight, or played too rough with another dog and cut her leg when they called me - they are animals after all. I would have understood - especially because she wasn't seriously injured. What really bothered me was that they made up some lame excuse and lied about what really happened. After two negative experiences I was on the fence about whether or not to send her back. I started asking around and heard mixed things. Some people said they loved it, but several people told me they had similar experiences to mine. Someone also told me about a horrifying incident at P&C that they had seen on the news about a year ago. It's not my story to tell so I won't, but if you search you will find it. That was the icing on the cake for me. My dog is by no means my "baby," but I'm not going to send her back to a place that isn't safe.

text: Regular readers know of my love for all things Han Chiang and his empire of Han Dynasty restaurants. So when I heard former managers Kevin and Catherina Huang opened up a spin-off in Rittenhouse, I had to check it out. The connection? Catherina Huang is Han's sister! Sure the Sichuan dishes are all there, but how does DanDan set itself apart from Han Dynasty? In a nutshell, the spice level seems tempered for the Rittenhouse crowd. And to be frank, the GF was all about that because unlike me, she can't handle the heat! I kid, I kid, but let's go on it with it shall we? Dan Dan Noodles [$7.95] Han Chiang has "famously" (jokingly?) stated that he didn't trust Westerners with mixing their own noodles. So in similar fashion, DanDan mixes the noodles tableside for you as well! Toothsome with great texture, the dish had sweetness from the peanut dressing, with some light spice that hits you in the back of your throat. Could have used a bit more of the crisp pork bits and I'd personally opt for more spice, but this was perfect for the GF. And for less than $8, it's quite the portion. Ask for a bowl of rice and this could easily be lunch with leftovers to boot. Fried Vegetable Potstickers [$6.95] The potstickers were great, with a nicely crisp exterior despite a wonderfully gluttonous wrapper and a good melange of veggies within. The dipping sauce was sweet with a lightly spicy kick. Pork Belly [$9.95] Sweet garlic chili oil Obviously, I had to try DanDan's take on the pork belly app I love. These were spot on with a huge portion of thinly sliced roast pork belly. The chili oil was more sweet than hot and provided the necessary seasoning for the pork. With a bowl of rice, I was pretty much set. Cumin Pork [$12.95] Stir fried, bell peppers, dried peppers, onions, cilantro We also decided to try the cumin pork, which featured lusciously porcine strips crusted with cumin. This was mixed with onions and bell peppers with bite, with the spice coming through from the dried Sichuan peppers. The cilantro provided a nicely herbaceous element to the dish DanDan's a great addition to the Rittenhouse area and is certainly tailored towards the neighborhood's tastes. That's not to say that they can't bump up the spice level to meet your Sichuan-spice needs! And the service? Wonderful! Our server Cati was extremely knowledgeable and friendly. DanDan should be getting their liquor license soon and their first floor is centered around the bar. It'll likely be a hot spot for happy hour, with a side of their eponymous noodles!

text: I was excited to at the idea of Thai/Mexican fusion - this particular pairing seemed like it would yield exciting, flavorful and quirky combinations. So, when Tuk Tuk first opened, I ordered delivery. We got some tacos, tres leches and something else (I don't quite remember). Unfortunately, even though I live within a 5 minute drive/10 minute bike ride, the food took about an hour to arrive and was stone cold. Not the best situation for tacos. They were ok, and I gave them a pass because they must have had delivery issues and so I didn't want to hold the cold tacos against them. Tonight, we were starving and having read about their new ramen dish on a recent Philly food blog, I thought it was time to give Tuk Tuk another chance. I was worried about delivery times though, so we ordered pick up. The ramen must have been a short lived special, since they no longer had it. So, instead we ordered Thai Chili Lamb Mole ($18), Strip Bass & Basil Fried Rice ($15) and Lemongrass Cinnamon Chipotle Bread Pudding ($7). All of this sounds amazing, right? Exactly the answer to one's craving for intense flavor, right? Well, neither of the main dishes tasted like anything. They have so many interesting ingredients, but literally did not taste like much. I'm not saying they didn't taste like a dish from Circles, but actually like a dish without any flavor at all; in a blind tasting, you'd say you were eating boiled rice :( We added salt and squeezed some lemon over both main dishes and so they tasted a little brighter, a little lemony, but that's it. And we paid $33 for them. The bread pudding was fine; it was moist and tasted like bread pudding, with a chili aftertaste - that was the chipotle, not especially integrated, and just an add on. Having spent almost $50 tonight on a dinner that was beyond disappointing, I can't recommend Tuk Tuk at all. I've had my fair share of so-so dinners, but $50 for this really added insult to injury. Maybe they don't think Sunday night service is worth spending much time on, so we got dishes that were thrown together but this was really a poor showing.

If you can, their hot chocolate is literally the best I've tasted in the U.S.! They also have a variety of delicious fancy teas, and Kombucha on tap (I haven't tried that yet though!). I know my review is super long, but I love this place, and that it exists in Tucson. I had at least three of my wedding celebration related gatherings here, and take all my out of town friends/family here to impress them with what our town has to offer! They always have special menus or treats for holidays, and it's kid friendly. Prep & Pastry is a gem, and I want everyone to go so that it stays open for a very long time!

text: Sbraga is easily one of my new favorite restaurants in Philly. For a restaurant with such creative dishes and high caliber of execution, the price was surprisingly reasonable ~$55 for (foie gras!) soup, an appetizer, a pasta dish, an entrée, and dessert. The service was also excellent, capping off a perfect dinner experience. The menu at Sbraga is truly international, with influences spanning from Mexico to Italy to Greece. We were worried that the meal might not be cohesive, but our dishes all ended up complementing each other quite nicely. We loved the tartare - the cumin yogurt made a punchy accompaniment to the lamb while the bibb lettuce kept it light and fresh. The saffron spaghetti, with its enticing combination of creamy saffron sauce and crab with a hint of spice, was our party's favorite dish of the night. For entrées, we ordered the cornish hen and seabream. the cornish hen was tender and juicy with a nice Spanish twist. Though I was a little concerned that the tzakziki sauce would overwhelm the delicate flavor of the seabream, Sbraga perfectly balanced the sweetness of the bream with the tartness of the tzakziki sauce. The service was outstanding - our waiter, Ylli, was friendly and attentive, recommending excellent wine and food choices. He also emphatically endorsed the chocolate tart - which was truly decadent and delicious, the perfect way to end a stellar meal. (If it's your birthday definitely let them know! My party neglected to mention it was my birthday, but after reading other reviews, it seems that Sbraga really knows how to make a birthday special.)

text: I placed my first order with SPUD after receiving a promo code from one of their friendly representatives at a local food event. With a little bit of credit, I was free to try out SPUD's produce delivery with no hesitation and I'm pleased to say that I'm quite impressed with my experience. My order consisted of mostly fruits and veggies but SPUD also offers baked goods, dairy, meat, juices and various other snacks. I was really impressed by their website's interface which made it easy to choose and review an order. Obviously it's challenging picking out produce online since you can't see the size, shape and colour of your choices but I was happy to try a little bit of everything as part of my first order. The quality of the produce was generally quite good and the order was delivered in a hefty box right to my door. Most of the produce was fresh, large and tasty, however a couple items were a little bit over-ripe. Given how important seeing and touching produce is when you buy it at the store or the market, I was generally quite impressed with what I had delivered and I would definitely use SPUD's services again, especially for heartier items like potatoes, onions, squash and packaged goods. SPUD is a really great resource for people who want to have fresh, organic food delivered but can't make it to the grocery store or won't be able to make it to one of Edmonton's markets on the weekends. It can be tough not being able to see and feel your produce before ordering it online but my first experience has assured me that they pick out great food to deliver to your door.

The menu is the most extensive I've ever seen, with an entire listing of brunch food (probably 30+ items, ranging from Croque Madame to Eggs Benedict to Open-Faced burritos to the more adventurous offerings) and the backside of the menu filled with different omelet choices and sandwiches. The brunch menu is slightly expensive, but definitely worth every dollar, as all the platters have a variety of foods (most come with fruit, salad, hash browns, and eggs) and the plates expertly crafted. The owner of the cafe is extremely friendly, as are the waitresses, and there is ample room here for semi-large parties (at least 6?). I ordered the saumon fume a cheval, and my friend ordered the Parisian Za. Both came with generous heaps of fresh avocado, salmon rolls, and perfectly cooked eggs. I would certainly venture back on my next brunch date, to try another dish in a European-esque environment!

The mussels, which come in either a red or white sauce, are also a popular appetizer that my fellow diners raved about (I didn't try them since I ate about half the zucchini myself). As for entrees, the eggplant parm is actually better than similar dishes that I have tried at higher-end Italian restaurants, and the four cheese ravioli, which is served with a pesto alfredo sauce, is decadent yet delicious. And don't even get me started on dessert - I could eat their chocolate zuccotto cake for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. The portions are extremely reasonable, so you definitely get your money's worth. The "family style" option is something to consider if dining with four or more people, since you get to choose multiple appetizers, pastas, meats, and desserts, all of which are all-you-can-eat. The service could not have been better. Our waiter was friendly, attentive, and - most importantly - extremely patient with our party of eight, who took what felt like decades to order.

text: This little park is actually a 10 foot-wide sidewalk which starts on the north at Columbus Statue Park and ends at Gandy Boulevard to the south. That makes this 4.5 mile-long hunk o' concrete the world's longest continuous sidewalk. The park hugs the perimeter of Hillsborough Bay, and follows Bayshore Boulevard around South Tampa. Most of us know this area because of the awesome scenic views of the Bay, the spectacular homes along Bayshore Boulevard, and that big ol' honkin' pirate ship. Whatttttt ?!?!?!? Bayshore Park is a popular spot to see people walking, jogging, running, pushing strollers, riding bikes, inline skating, and dog walking, as they gaze over the sea wall and watch for signs of manatee and dolphins and pirates! Trail amenities include benches, a water fountain, bicycle parking, a city marina and fitness stations. The sunrises and sunsets are world-class, and just another reason why I'm glad that I live in Florida. In late January this section of Tampa is home to the legendary Gasparilla Pirate Invasion and Pirate Parades. Any good student of Tampa history will tell you that the name of Tampa's traditional Gasparilla Carnival comes from legendary pirate Jose Gaspar, "last of the Buccaneers," who terrorized the coastal waters of West Florida during the late 18th and early 19th century. Gaspar, given to calling himself "Gasparilla," served as a lieutenant in the Royal Spanish Navy for five years until 1783 when, upon seizing command of a Spanish sloop-of-war, he with his fellow mutineers set sail for the Florida straits. And so the young Spanish aristocrat-turned-pirate began an adventurous life as outlaw of the sea. The story of the swashbuckling Gasparilla was unearthed and his memory revived in 1904 when Tampa's social and civic leaders adopted the pirate as patron rogue of their city-wide celebration. The Gasparilla Children's Parade comes first with hundreds and hundreds of pint-sized Johnny Depp look-alike swashbucklers taking to Bayshore Boulevard and cheering on all of the floats, marching bands, and dance companies. Most everyone is in costume, and hoping to snag some pirate's booty (strands of beads) to take home and show Mom and Dad. The following weekend is the raucous and outrageous Gasparilla Pirates Invasion and Parade. This time the pirate ships sail up through Hillsborough Bay to the Convention Center where the pirates demand the keys to the City from the Mayor. From there the costumed pirates lead the parade floats, marching bands, dance teams, along the same route as they cheer for grog, beads, and wenches! No matter when you come to visit Bayshore Park you're guaranteed to have a great time. Enjoy the view, the warm weather, the sunsets, and let loose with a mighty "Arrrggghhh!"

text: Let me start by saying that I had been wanting to try Catch Twenty Three since my wife and I moved to Tampa. After nearly a year here we finally buckled down and went. We also ordered the Oysters Rockefeller as an appetizer. Again, it came out fairly quickly. The oysters weren't bad, not great, but not bad. They were properly cleaned and seasoned well. For our entrées my wife ordered the Steak Diane, my mother the Filet Mignon, my father the Catch Salad with Shrimp and Mussels, and I ordered the Mixed Grill. Let me just say that the food was mediocre at best. My wife loved the sauce over her steak but the steak itself was under seasoned. They did a great job, however, cooking the meats to our preferred doneness. My mother had no complaints about the Filet Mignon but didn't really have any praise for it either. My father, on the other hand, didn't care for his pasta dish. Said it was incredibly bland. The shrimp were rubbery and chewy from being severely overcooked. The mussels were just cold and tasteless. Finally, the Mixed Grill I had ordered started off promising. It comes with chicken, steak, and pork. The steak was seasoned and cooked very well. The chicken was primarily seasoned with aromatic seasoning, so not a lot of, "in your face", flavor. The chicken was also cooked perfectly. It has the right tenderness to it and it was very juicy. The pork is where it starts to get scary. The meat was horribly undercooked to the point it was almost raw in the center. Needless to say I didn't eat much of that. From what I did taste in my first bite, though, the pork had been seasoned slightly and covered in sauce. This place seems to use their sauces to hide the fact that their food isn't worth the hefty prices they charge. My father has been sick for the last three days after our dinner here. He's been vomiting and has had moderate diarrhea. My wife had diarrhea the rest of the night after dinner but felt fine the next day. Luckily, my mother and I were spared from any would-be illnesses that could've come from Catch Twenty Three. Overall, the food, that of it that wasn't under or over cooked, was mediocre at best. The drinks were poorly put together and tasted awful. The staff was polite and timely with our food, but at what cost? I won't be going back to Catch Twenty Three. I give this a 1 out of 5 rating. text: I don't usually post reviews but I thought this deserved one because this was by far the worst restaurant experience I've ever had in my entire life. My family and I were so excited to try this place out especially after hearing so many good things about it. My family and I are also sushi lovers, traveling all the way to Japan to try the real thing. Please trust me when I say, we know and LOVE sushi. We drove up to Jersey from Philly just to try this place out. We arrived on a weekend, and when we walked in it was crowded. We waited about 15 minutes to be seated. We ordered sushi and sashimi for five as well as a few extra rolls on the side. We had a feeling that it would take a little longer than most sushi restaurants we had been to just because of how crowded it was that night. And so we waited.... The first 30 minutes went by with no sign of our food, but we gave the restaurant the benefit of the doubt. So we didn't say anything. Then the next 30 minutes rolled by. One of the side rolls came out. Even in our hungry state, the rolls we got weren't that great. At least not up to the hype and pretty much at the standard of any other sushi restaurant. Also, By this time we had waited a full hour and people who had been seated about the same time as us were finishing up their meals. We decided to notify the waitress politely (we are a very non confrontational bunch). She was incredibly sweet and apologetic. No problem, we were willing to wait a little more. Another 30 min go past and we are still wondering where our sushi is :(. Even people who were seated after us are leaving because they already finished. I understood we had a rather big order with 5 people, but an hour and a half is a rather long wait... We notified our waitress again and she was once again very apologetic. Even her co-worker who wasn't working our table said she was sorry. So we nodded, although getting pretty impatient. Finally another 30 min go by and we just couldn't take it any more. After waiting for 2 hours, we just decided to tell the waitress we were leaving. She apologized again and again, but at this point we were just frustrated and starving. Honestly, I don't think would be so upset with this place if it were just the wait. But here's the kicker, there's a sushi alas behind where the the rows of tables are and the chef/boss wasn't preparing anything our last thirty minutes there, just washing his cutting board. And not only that but some woman who appeared to either be his worker or wife tried to get him to speed up but he just shoved her aside and kept washing his board. He even looked at our table and ignored us. I've never seen my dad so upset with a restaurant and I've never left so disappointed. We just ended up grabbing McDonald's on the way back. But boy, was that a bad experience. Hopefully this serves as a fair warning for everyone else out there. Or maybe it was a fluke. All I know is that this is one place I would never return to. 1) because the sushi is just average and 2) because the service is slower than a blind turtle that only had two functioning legs :/

text: OK, so what could make a delicious traditional Brazilian rodizio of meats even better? If you guessed bacon, you would be right. Since living in salt lake city, the rodizio grill has been my favorite restaurant. I went to it for the first time in 1999, right before I went to live in Rio de Janeiro. The rodizio grill is a great representation of a traditional Brazilian Churrascaria and is my favorite place to go to make me feel like I'm in Brazil again . I would also say that the Nashville installment is even better than the one in Utah. Now, back to bacon. When I went in January it was Bacon month, and there were several more of the meats that hat been paired with bacon. Also, at the salad bar there were several different local bacons for you to try. The jalapeño bacon was especially good. If that weren't enough, the pao de queijo also had bits of bacon in it. When we were offered refills on the delicious little cheese breads, we were given both the original version and some more of the bacon ones. They came right out of the oven, and were perfect. The rodizio of meats brought many different varieties. They seemed to have the perfect combinations of degrees of wellness. My wife was able to get the well done pieces she wanted and I could get the more medium rare pieces. Most of our choices were also the "first cut" pieces, which are the best. They are the ones who've been exposed directly to the fire and salted directly. I'll still say that the picanha is my favorite. The staff was great and brought us the few meats we wanted to try again at the end of our meal. I want to say Anna was our server's name and she did a great job. For the first time, we also got desert. The brigadeiro cake was an enormous portion that we shared and still only got half way through. It was delicious and reminded me of the Brazilian bakeries in Rio. We were extremely happy with our meal here and will continue to frequent regularly.

text: Delicioso. Like, that really is all you need to know. The atmosphere is vibrant--colorful, a bit more rustic than the kitschy, common Mexican themed places so many of us are beyond used to these days. It's quite a large restaurant with even more banquet/dining space upstairs, which I presume they reserve for parties and the like. From the outside, you can't miss it. I've never been to Colombia or any other South or Latin American country, but I have been in and around North Philly. This place pops out and says "Hola!" to your eyes as you ride down N. 5th in the midst of all the other typical storefronts and corner stores. Y'all. Get all the sangrias. Scrumptious. Yes, I tried them all--the blanco, the riojo and the durazno (laden with plump peaches). A pitcher of one of them is a must. They also make a mean apple martini. And yes, I appreciate my beverages. I got the Happy Hour empanada special and the buffalo wings. The empanadas were crisp and delectable. The special consists of the cheese, chicken, shrimp and ground beef with potato empanadas. For my main course I ordered the Churrasco Argentino and it was grilled to perfection. I hardly needed my knife! I complimented this slab of deliciousness with yellow rice, red beans and incredibly fresh avocado. There was enough for me to take home for lunch the following day and I enjoyed it just as much as I had the night before. Our server, Anthony, was absolutely darlin' to our party of 4. They happily accommodated our request for a larger table and gave the type of service that ensured we were never thirsty or hungry. text: Finch and Fork has really evolved into an essential part of Santa Barbara fine dining scene since James Siao took over the kitchen. It is much better than the typical hotel restaurant. Service is good, the atmosphere is comfortable, the bar turns out high quality cocktails, and the food is always delectable. I had dinner here on Friday and enjoyed the whole experience. Thick hearty pork chop was grilled to medium doneness so it was juicy and tender, paired with sweet butternut puree, and warm spicy ginger flavor crumbles. Dry packed scallops were seared to a silky medium rare, placed on top of corn salsa and guacamole, further enhanced with grapefruit sections and chorizo vinaigrette. The salt and pepper chicken wings could use a little more salt. The glaze was the same as the glaze in pork ribs and pickled watermelon dish (available during the summer months), sweet, spicy, and savory. A few pieces of pickled celery cuts through the greasiness of fried food. The mac and cheese was made with mornay sauce and bacon, topped with extra cheese so it baked up crunchy and bubbling. My favorite dessert is the toasted banana shake, this and the budino from Olio are two of my favorite desserts in Santa Barbara. The only miss of the night was the sticky toffee cake. It was dry as if it was heated a few minutes too long. The menu changes with season. I have had the pork cheek with gnocchi, grilled ribs with pickled watermelon, sunchoke smear with smoked salmon, and grilled steak with chimichurri sauce. They were all delicious and the only less than stellar dish I had here was the halibut in a mountain of frisee, which was axed from the menu and hadn't returned since the early days of Finch and Fork.

text: Generally, I'd call this an OK mid-range hotel, with an acceptable location not too far away from anything worth visiting in the New Orleans area. I have but a few notes that justify my two-star review: 1. The AC in our room was problematic. It'd be fine one night, then the next we'd notice that it just wasn't cooling. We'd notify the front desk, someone would "fix" it, then it'd be fine for a night. The next night, I'm sweating again near 80 degrees. 2. Beware the woman you'll be shuttled off to just after check-in. She'll act incredibly friendly, and try to give you all kinds of helpful recommendations. You'll be invited to a free "breakfast" that supposedly "all our guests like to take advantage of." It's at 9:30AM, and all you have to do is let them know which day you want to come to this lovely breakfast. Don't be fooled. It's a timeshare presentation. Now, if you want to make $50-75 via gift card for sitting through their presentation, it is possible to do so. We were able to get $75, but it was a hard-earned $75. It required a lot of sticking to our guns and just saying "No." I think of timeshare presentations as affairs I can just snooze through, while someone plays a half-hour long video. How I wish that had been the case. Here at the Wyndham, the presentation is a "workshop" format, as they called it. You will be assigned one salesman, and he/she will sit there with you for nearly one hour, asking questions, stroking your ego, and telling you how great and extensive the Wyndham network is. We politely declined after all this, thinking it'd be over. It wasn't. In car-dealership fashion, another salesman was brought in. Decline. They brought in the GENERAL MANAGER to give us the hard sell....they truly do not plan to let you leave there without buying a timeshare. We were there for 90 minutes, at which point we'd had more than enough and just wanted to get on with our day. We made up an excuse of having somewhere to be, and finally wriggled free of the cadre of salespeople that had descended upon us like vultures. We did get our $75 gift card. Knock yourselves out, if you believe this kind of high-pressure sell to be worth the reward. I might do it again, as it was nice to be able to plop down the gift card at one of the many New Orleans restaurants...but then again, I'm good at being an obstinate pain in the ass and saying "no," repeatedly. If you are not good at saying No.....you're going to end up having purchased a timeshare. Don't say I didn't warn you. Just walk away from the woman at check-in who is being unnaturally nice. Just. Walk. Away. I don't necessarily have a problem with a timeshare presentation, but they out-and-out LIE as to what you're getting yourself into. They lie about their intent, and then once you're there, they lie about how long it takes. 3. This place is valet-only, and it's $20 a day, paid in advance. I have a legendary hatred of valet parking, but since we had a rental car, I sucked it up and dealt with the expense and inconvenience. What this hotel does NOT tell you, is that there *is* street parking within a block or two, and it's fairly ample. In fact, I'd say you stand an excellent chance of parking within 3 blocks. If you don't mind walking a little, this is an option. If I was staying here again, I'd probably opt to just try parking on the street. 4. The bed was spacious, but uncomfortable. Between my discomfort and the warm room, I spent my relaxing vacation in a state of poor rest and fatigue. After having written all that, I'm kind of wondering why I'm not giving this hotel one star.....but hey, the location *is* excellent. I suppose that's worth something.

text: I am a frequent visitor to New Orleans and dine at its best restaurants when I can. My family and I were with a group of 12 family and friends for a special occasion dinner at Emeril's Delmonico on a recent Saturday. Considering Emeril's reputation--and prices--it was a very disappointing experience. We had an 8:15 reservation and were seated at a long table better suited for 8 than 12; our chairs were literally touching. Not getting any help from the wait staff, we took it upon ourselves to move 2 people to the ends of the table and adjust our place settings. Staff said they could not adjust the table further. Worse than that, the table was directly under an AC vent blowing cold air on a high setting. We had to ask three times over the course of an hour to have the AC turned down before it finally was taken care of. 8:30 passed before we were approached by a waiter who gave us water. About 15 minutes later a waiter asked about drinks. Of course, we said! Several guests wanted white wine so we ordered a bottle of white wine (on their menu), only to wait 20 minutes because the staff said the wine needed to be chilled! However, the biggest problem was that the dining room was too noisy to carry on conversation. Maybe it's that way most of the time, but that night there was an extremely loud table of eight. A table of four between our table and the boisterous one actually left on account of the noise. I know the reason because I joined them as they spoke with management. But Wet we were stuck - I knew that the chances of finding another table for 12 in New Orleans on a Saturday night were nil. I asked the manager why the restaurant would let a group to so completely disrupt the experience for others, but the manager was unwilling to ask them to quiet down a bit. Not the Emeril's attention to detail I'm familiar with. Once the loud group left, the experience improved. The food measured up. But the experience left us with a bad feeling about the Emeril's brand, and I know I won't be going back to an Emeril's restaurant again. Details matter and this night, this restaurant did not measure up. There are better more reliable options. Rod Kuckro Alexandria, VA

I will admit that I tend to avoid rib joints because, well, I don't actually like ribs. Actually, to be more accurate I'm a slightly spastic paraplegic who abhors the mess I make when I try to eat ribs. It would be sort of like placing Pigpen inside a pig pen. Ya know? Anyway, as I've learned over the years, it seems to be true that most rib joints actually have foods other than ribs and, in fact, I tend to like those other foods like pulled pork, brisket, chicken, and a variety of other sandwiches and meals. So, on a rainy day in Indianapolis with the temperature rising and my energy depleted I decided to go ahead and venture over for my first visit to GT South's. To look at GT South's, you'd probably think to yourself it's just a little divey hole-in-the-wall (which actually fits rib joints anyway). Actually, you'd kind of be right. It's located in a small strip center with at least one other restaurant, a bar, and I believe another business. There's also a police sub-station next door, so I'd avoid any temptation to act out. They have a single accessible parking spot, but they do have a wheelchair ramp and the one spot does meet ADA requirements. I'd actually stopped into GT South's a week or so ago, but I didn't see the spot and didn't end up stopping. So, it's good to know it's there and actually is clearly marked. They have a double-sided entry that is pretty manageable, but the staff was obviously paying attention despite my arrival on the early side of the dinner hour. I was greeted at the door and helped right away to a four-top table where the server removed two chairs to allow room for the wheelchair. I was rather tickled to be seated right beneath this really awesome print of hands that I just fell in love with while dining. My server, Kristi, was incredibly warm and friendly and I learned quite a bit about the restaurant before also learning that she's also part of the family that owns the restaurant. Because they also offer catering, they have a staff of right around 35 and it was a nice plus to be able to meet someone within the family because I think that always gives you a sense of the business. The GT South's decor is quite simple, but warm. If you require lots of polish and shine, you'll probably find yourself checking the silverware to see if it's clean, but the older establishment is warm and well cared for with a main dining area, a private dining area, and a middle section that looked like where you did take out orders, etc. I ordered my usual unsweetened iced tea and it was brought to the table in a timely manner. After deliberating a little bit, I opted for a pulled pork sandwich. It comes with chips along with one side - I chose cole slaw among choices that also included mac n' cheese, red potatoes, apple sauce, turnip greens cornbread, and a few others. I didn't see any sort of upgrade options (like turning the chips into fries), but the sandwich itself came as regular for $6.95 or jumbo for an extra dollar. I hadn't eaten lunch, so I opted for the jumbo. The pulled pork was definitely on the upper tier of pulled pork sandwiches that I've had locally. Kristi offered me samples of both the mild and hot bbq sauces. I tried both and definitely preferred the hot - it was hot, but not too hot. The meat was flavorful, tender, and really lingered on my palate in just the right way. The bun initially seemed like a generic bun, but it was large enough for the sandwich and seemed to be lightly toasted. It complemented the flavor without dominating it. The cole slaw was also very good, though folks who prefer ultra-creamy cole slaw might be a touch disappointed. I like cole slaw that allows me to taste all of its ingredients and this decent-sized cup definitely did. With the entire meal right around $11, it was definitely a good meal at a good price and I would definitely order it again. I am knocking off one star for one fairly significant faux pas in my world - I didn't get offered an iced tea refill despite lingering a few minutes after my meal and the glass being empty. There are times I'd actually knock down even another star for that, because my refills are truly that important. That said, the service was otherwise terrific and the food was definitely higher than 3-star food. When a drink is right around $2.50, it's not unreasonable to expect at least one refill without having to ask. Have you ever visited a restaurant where you just instantly felt comfortable? That's how I felt at GT South's, where even the customers were friendly. I really liked it here, not because it was razzle-dazzle, but because I had a good meal and felt welcome!

text: Layout: Sandpiper has a decent layout. Obviously, the track benefits from its location. While most of the property is flat, it's northern portion does have some nice contour which sets up for an excellent 10th hole, which in my opinion is the top hole on the property. It is an interesting hole, potentially driveable with the right wind. The green is very narrow, multitiered, and perched on a small cliff. Even a perfect drive to just in front of the green often yields a par, particularly when the pin is back. The 11th is also a dramatic hole, a downhill par 3 measuring over 200 yards to a narrow green with the beach behind and to the left. The rest of the course is pretty straightforward. The par 5's are basic and fairly easy (the first hole is probably the strongest). The second hole is the toughest on the course, a 450 yard par 4 with a very tight drive lined by trees. Overall, it's a very scoreable track, a place where you can really go low if you are on your game. Conditioning: While I recognize that the drought has hit a lot of the California courses hard, Sandpiper is in terrible shape. I have played it multiple times in previous years, including 2014 when the drought had begun to affect courses, and it was in much better shape. The fairways are sparse, and have been invaded by all sorts of native grasses. They have been trying to water the course, but are doing so in a bizarre fashion, with standing water puddles in fairways. The bunkers are horrible, and largely unkept. Some are packed mud, others fluffy thin sand, none raked or cared for. The greens were punched and heavily sanded (see below) just days before I played so were essentially unputtable. Previous times I played, the greens were decent. Difficulty: Sandpiper is an easy course, and wildly oversloped. There are many very easy holes. It would be much more difficult if they could grow out the junk, but since it is all dead, you can hit the ball all over the property with impunity. Value: Incredibly overpriced. Even if it was in decent shape, it is overpriced at 185 with a cart (for a Friday), but in its current condition, that is a laughable rate. If I lived in the area, there is no way I would pay that rate to play this course. It's conditioning is below that which would be expected at a muni. Furthermore, I called to make my time one week prior and was travelling from out of state. They did not inform me that they were going to be punching and working on the greens. In fact, DURING MY ROUND, they were dragging greens - greens that were already unplayable. I was hitting approaches to greens over maintenance crews. I usually don't mind this sort of stuff, and would have still considered playing there even with the punch, but there should be a discount and they need to clearly inform the players that this will be the case. It was an absolute joke. Walkability: Easy walk. Course is made to walk and you should walk it if you are physically able. Scenery: Wonderful scenery with great views. A little close to the highway, but the noise is only present on a few holes. Practice Facility: Acceptable. Sandpiper offers so much potential due to its location and playability. It is not an overly difficult track and could provide a great golfing experience. Unfortunately it is incredibly overpriced and in horrible shape. I can understand distressed fairways due to the drought, but the atrocious bunker care exemplifies the poor maintenance that is going on here. I have played many courses at this price point, and this would be the worst one, even were it not for greens punched and actively being worked on/dragged during my round. To not warn me of that ahead of time and not offer a discount is laughably bad. I was skeptical of the situation there after reading recent reviews, but it far exceeded my expectations - in a negative sense. I would consider returning due to the location and chance to shoot a low score, but only after I have confirmed they have gotten their act together. 4 out of 10 at best right now, could be 8.5 or better if not for the mess they have made of it.

text: I have lived in the Indianapolis area since 1999, and believe it or not, I have never been to this cafeteria until recently. In the interim, I had heard so much about how good of a place it is to eat,......especially how awesome their pies are. Unfortunately, the wait was just short of worth it. We went on a Thursday evening, and it was fairly busy enough. With most cafeterias it's like a cattle line/chute or call,.....you stand in line, moving along quickly as you point out what you want to eat, they put it on your plate, move on to the register at the end of the line, pay for your food, and then go find a table/seat. The food service line was efficient enough, but the servers seemed to be unfocused, preoccupied and lackadaisical. I tried to ask if I could have a little whipped cream on my apple pie, and it seemed to be a miserable chore to one gal to accommodate me. We found a table after paying, and thankfully the gal who was tending the floor and checking drinks - was nice. It's always a plus when servers can muster up a smile whether they like their job or not. We got the fried chicken, because I had read on previous reviews that it was very good. I will totally concur with that assessment. Everything else was nothing to write home about - including the canned green beans, processed mac and cheese, mashed potatoes, and the hush puppies. I actually had to send the hush puppies back because they a very weird/odd taste to them that I couldn't pin point. I got a refund on those. I am only giving them ** 2 stars because of the fried chicken and the apple pie I had. Those two items are really what saved them. Otherwise the rest of the menu had quite a bit to be desired. I have had similar quality and tasting food at any other food line cafeteria and/or buffet I have ever been to like - ex: Ryan's, Golden Coral, etc,... If I would have chosen a buffet style -all you can eat - restaurant, I surely would have gotten more food or choices for the all mighty dollar as well. When all was said and done, our bill came to over $30 for two people. I think that's a little high and excessive considering the quality and the amount of food that we received. You're not paying for atmosphere in that place either, that's for sure! I sure wish the value and quality would make it worthwhile when eating out these days. It's just another sad commentary to the fact that great restaurants are really far and few in between anymore. Most are just a 'slop it out at you' dime/dine a dozen. I am not sure how most good sized families can afford to eat out at family style restaurants today. It seriously costs a small fortune to do so. It just would be nice to get something satisfying and worthwhile for one's money for a change. It really wasn't worth the drive when it was all said and done. It's safe to say I will not be going back

Anyway, like I said, don't expect the 1/2 lb of beans to be enough for more than 2 people because you're sure not getting that much. 3. Food - Aside from the meat, everything there is fair to bad. We ordered sweet potatoes this time and got chewy, partially cooked, room temp chunks of sweet potato... I honestly don't know how they can serve that kind of stuff and hope for people to come back. The potato wedges (from the first trip) were also memorably room temp and undercooked. I love bbq and I really hope these guys can get it together a little more. She wrote me a script to go be tested for asthma AFTER I try a SAMPLE of Breo Ellipta (a steroid that is inhaled) for two weeks. I was also prescribed a canister of Albuterol. Well within 48 hours I was in the emergency room because I felt as thought my throat had closed entirely. Nobody in the ER was familiar with Breo Ellipta and they told me to immediately stop taking it. They did some asthma testing there and I was testing negative. They sent me to see a pulmologist on the Main Line (the same one my mom sees). He was shocked she gave me Breo Ellipta to take. 1. I tested negative for asthma. 2. ITS A MEDICATION USED FOR COPD PATIENTS. 3. It is specifically not to be given to asthma patients. I saw a new doctor, she diagnosed me with anxiety and I have been doing great ever since. I have looked into suing McPherson for medical malpractice. She has not idea what she is doing.

text: I am a big believer in the Yelp universe because of the reliability of reviews so while I was amazed at the number of outstanding reviews for Restaurante Yesenia, and I love to support small family-owned businesses, I would not be doing anyone favors if I didn't write honestly about my experience. First of all - everything I read about the attitude of the service was spot-on. Very nice and helpful. The dining area was small, intimate and reminiscent of being in south america with the decor and flags and small freezer full of helados. So why two stars... we had a large group of 15 and called in advance to ensure enough seating. The first of us arrived 5-10 minutes before 6:00 (our reservation) and by the time we were all seated, we ordered at around 6:10 (before anyone else in the restaurant). We did not get our food until 6:50. My guess is that our server was new or in training. It was weird. He took our food orders first, then went away, then came back a few minutes later to take drink orders but for only half the table before disappearing. A long time passed before we had to ask for our drinks - they eventually served ice water and two soursop smoothies and we had to remind them that we also ordered beer. So it got off to a bad start - drinks should not be that complicated or delayed. I don't think we saw our server again because the owner came out to deliver our entrees. Unfortunately, several of our orders were wrong - and some dishes came out that no one ordered. About three dishes, including my papusas had to be exchanged and dishes for two people came very late (one was enchiladas that should have been pork, but was chicken - my friend who ordered did not say anything since it had been so long a wait, he was too hungry to wait any more). The food - I was ready to give the benefit of the doubt: large party, perhaps new server, okay but the food is to die for, right? I'm struggling here because I'm not seeing five stars at all. The papusas - are crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside - fresh - but I think it was difficult to identify the pork or stomach flavor/texture, because the cheese overwhelms the rest of the papusa. I ordered the Sopa de Pollo - good, not great, and on the salty side. Chicken was dry. Since we had to wait so long for the food, I got to know the chips and salsa very well - mouthwatering, crispy and home made. Salsa was killer - fresh and spicy. The fish - my daughter ordered this and I tried it and liked it - the portion was large, meaty and well seasoned. My experience was two stars (I've experienced better) because of the waiting time, ordering snafus and hit or miss food items. This doesn't mean I wouldn't try it again, and I think I will because they are friendly and the reviews are so good. For now, I do have to call it like I see (and taste) it.
label: NEG

text: The two-star caption says it all: "Meh. I've experienced better." Oink isn't awful, but it's definitely not great, either. We went there for breakfast and got the full bacon flight, the bacon benedict, and an omelet, along with the different classic bloody mary and the Oink Bacon Bloody Mary. The drinks were bland: no spice, no zesty tang, no indication (in flavor or feeling) that there was in fact vodka in them. I really like bloody marys, so I was most disappointed in that. The bacon flight was the best part of the meal -- eight varieties of bacon, including hickory, honey, cured, and jalapeno. The jalapeno was definitely my favorite. It had a smoky heat and depth of flavor unlike anything else we ate or drank there today. Our entrees were fine. A bit on the greasy side, but okay. My main complaint for the bacon benedict was that it was absolutely drowned in hollandaise sauce, to the point that I was spooning it off just to get to the egg underneath. My fiance was similarly underwhelmed by his omelet, which he said was oddly dry. We didn't hate it, but we also don't plan on going back. As other reviewers have said, it's overpriced for what it is. Save your money and go to an unassuming diner. Oink is going to have to do better than this if it wants to stay in business.

I've also had the pizza and I don't know of a place that serves a better one. Incidentally. a comment about Erica's comment. text: We found Franks by just walking down the street. They have Johnny, a family member, calling attention to the Restaurant. We decided to try it the next day. I found the prices to be a bit high as the bulk was $100.oo for 2. Adding $38 for liqueur. That's the only reason they didn't get 5 stars. I'm also NOT comparing it to Chicago food, but for there.... It was my fav. With that said, it was enough and carried us through the day without that bloated feeling. I'm jonesing for that snapper right now!! Note: we had been told by many that it isn't that great of a place. In my opinion it appears that they steer you in other directions that I do not understand. The instructor (there's a bunch of them and they all ROCK) will tell you what kind of workout you will be doing- strength, training, or endurance...maybe a blend of em all! And then they get the music pumpin and you start the class! Most classes are an hour long and half the class is cardio, with the other half being weight training. So on your cardio block, you can either do walking, running, or jogging and you vary between your base pace, push pace, and your all-out pace. The instructors let you know when and for how long you will be at each pace and walk you through everything! For the weight-room, if you have any injuries or ailments they can modify any workout for you! text: A good friend asked if I was up for trying something "weird and tasty." Obviously, I agreed, and found myself with plans to try a sushi burrito. The entire drive to West Chester, BF and I debated what it would be like --- an oversized maki roll? A tortilla full of sushi rice and raw fish? Turns out, it's like perfection and combines some of the the best aspects of sushi and burritos. BF and I split an order of the fried shrimp shumai, which were excellent. For my meal, I tried the Bonzilla burrito, which combined spicy tuna with the crunch of shrimp tempura and cucumber into a perfect-sized burrito roll made on "tortilla paper," which is like a soft, thinner version of a tortilla. BF ordered the Bubba burrito, which I actually may have like just a teeny bit better --- the crunch of shrimp tempura with crab stick, avocado, and cucumber with a sweet, tangy honey-lime sauce. The burrito was just enough that I was able to finish it WITHOUT the discomfort associated with the typical burrito-sized food baby, but I was still happily full. I also felt like I was eating sushi, but at a cost of approx $10 per person. Of note, the place is tiny and probably seats about 10 people around a counter. Our group of 4 just barely managed to find seats together, and then only because a couple was kind enough to move down a bit. If you are lucky enough to find seating, you should know that it's BYOB! Very much looking forward to our next trek to West Chester!

text: I've been living back in Edmonton for just over a year now and I don't know why it took me so long to come to Tres Carnales. In the past 4 days I have been here 3 times, I think I have a serious problemo! This place is known for their authentic Mexican street food, and I'm willing to bet they are doing it right! I've never been to Mexico so I cannot vouch for Tres Carnales' authenticity; but I can tell you that it's some seriously good "street food". With this place around the corner from my pad, I don't think I need to go to Mexico! From the moment you walk in you immediately feel like family. The staff here tell you what to eat, tell you what to drink and tell you where to sit. If you've never been here before they will also tell you how much food you should order! Whether they are the ones cooking the food or the ones serving it... They make you feel comfortable and have no reservations about recommending something great; which incase you didn't know, is everything! Upon my first visit here the young lady behind the counter asked if I've been to Tres Carnales before. Having never enjoyed it before she briefly described the menu, going over what they have to offer and how it's served. She made some recommendations and told us what her fave was, which turned out to be mine too! They offer their Tacos with 8 different types of protein!! How one narrows that down to one is beyond me, I suggest trying 3 and sharing with a friend. In a serving you get 4 tacos and they're only just over $10. My favourite is called "Al Pastor" it's a shaved pork that's slightly sweet. Similar to a bacon in my opinion! Some other awesome options are Chorizo, Beef Brisket and a fish taco (haven't tried the fish, but some other diners were saying it was their fave!). They also have a few veggie/vegan options for the herbivores out there! The Tacos are served up very simply with onions and cilantro and lime on the side. Each variety comes with its own special sauce or salsa. I like the red one which I forget the name of... I could drink it! If tacos aren't your thing Tres Carnales also offers Quesadilla, Tortas (a huge sandwich) and other daily specials. On my second visit I was recommended the soup, which would have been perfect for that day but I was craving some tacos! The service here is amazing, friendly and you really couldn't ask for better! It has been spotless with no dirty tables on each of my visits which for a place as busy as this place gets says a lot. I can safely say I will be back many times!

text: We really want to like this place! I promise you that I normally have a pretty high tolerance for minor hiccups at a restaurant having been a server myself in college. I went with my family on a beautiful fall Sunday evening. The place has a cool feel both inside and out, with lots of space and interesting decor. We were promptly seated outside, but this was the only thing that could be described as prompt.. We sat unnoticed and without menus or silverware for at least 10-15 min. One waitress said she'd be right back, then another asked if we needed menus and beer list (yes, and duh, we're at a brewery). Finally we got menus and were able to quickly choose beer from the list. I had the Oktoberfest, which was just what I was looking for. Other beers at the table were the pilsner and the honey brown, both very good! We waited a while to put in our order, dishes were: Coop (chx sandwich with apples and gouda), fish and chips, and soup and salad. My chicken sandwich itself tasted good, though slightly over-cooked and chewy. The mayo that came in a small ramekin had clearly been sitting out for a while (portions on top were turning clear, ew). My cottage cheese side was completely room temperature and I didn't risk taking more than one bite. The soup came to the table luke warm which was requested to be warmed up. The fish and chips was just ok, breading fell off as eaten and they majorly skimped on fries. Finally the reheated soup came out piping hot (a little overkill in our opinion) about 5 whole min after being taken back. The server was nice enough, but I suspect she had tables inside and didn't have time to keep coming outside (giving benefit of doubt here). Given all the things that went wrong or weren't prepared right, especially since the place is new, I was really surprised not to see a manager circulating at all. We would have shared all of this with management, as we really liked the atmosphere of the place and want it to do well. It really looks like they have some kitchen management things to work out as well as whole staff training. I do hope they can make this all work! Will definitely be back and hope for a better experience deserving of more stars!

When I walked into the boutique style storefront located just next door to Saint Louis Bread Company and Pi Pizza he was there solo and in the middle of making a delicious looking batch of macaroons. Not wanting to interrupt the process I told myself just look around, grab a few pieces and jet. I was there nearly 20 minutes just talking to Rick about chocolate, the assembly line production, local businesses he whole sales to and process of placing custom orders. Rick walked me through every piece of chocolate in the shop; describing the ingredients and making my mouth water lol...I could sense his intense passion for chocolate in every word. He also pointed out the several pieces of equipment used to make his chocolate which comes straight from the coffee bean by the way. There was one truffle in particular I had to have (Dark Chocolate with Goat Cheese) I love all things goat cheese and all things dark chocolate so this was a definite must have. I also left with some dark chocolate with lavender, ginger, hazelnut and a cute little baggie of vanilla macaroons. Interior has a beautifully chic yet simple decor. The lighting was especially nice. text: For a special occasion, be sure to get a booth For this visit my wife made reservations for us on open table.com for our 12th wedding anniversary. When we arrived we were greeted by the hostess who took our last name, fiddled around for what seemed like two or three minutes, and then asked us to follow her to our table. We were situated in what was basically the middle of the room on a four top. Before we sat down, my wife and I actually teetered on whether or not we should request a booth or not, but we ultimately remained seated at this table thinking that the restaurant must have been full which is why we ended up with this table. Later we would discover that we were completely incorrect on that assumption and that we could have been given a much more romantic booth. We would also later learn that this restaurant actually has about a dozen secluded booths which we discovered on our way out, poking our heads into different rooms as we made our way to the door. Honestly, I found that to be truly inexcusable as we purposely made the restaurant aware that we were there for our anniversary several times over. We started the evening with the pear and brie cheese fondue and a bottle of the Mirassou Pinot Noir for $30. The wine is a fairly decent bottle which would normally set you back $10 in the store. It has strawberry undertones and we found it to be quite delightful for our meal. The fondue was served with a small bowl of vegetables including mostly cauliflower, followed by celery, and carrots. In another bowl we found Granny Smith apples and lastly a large bowl of sliced bread, which was a mixture of French and a couple of pieces of wheat/French bread. I would suggest asking for just bread during this phase of your meal as the other items do not allow you to actually experience the wonderful blend of cheeses and pears. In fact, I'd venture to say that the vegetables will actually leave you scratching your head as to why they are served in the first place. We decided not to get any salads, and instead move directly to entrées. It is suggested that you get two or three of the entrée choices to make up each individuals meal. While I found this to be spot on in terms of portion size, I do have a few suggestions. My wife and I each ordered filet mignon, and I ordered the lobster tail and my wife ordered the shrimp as our second entrées. I am going to guess that the portion sizes for each plate are around 4 ounces. We both found the fillets to be perfect cuts of meat. The lobster tail was cut into four pieces and was very strangely sprinkled with some sort of red granular spice that neither of us could identify. This seemed to detract from the overall taste of the lobster so much so that for my second piece I actually dumped it in my water glass and swirled it around until most of that "red seasoning" was absent. Then and only then did the lobster actually taste like lobster. Overall for the $9.50 you pay for the lobster tail I'd recommend skipping it. Same was true unfortunately for the shrimp as well. You only get three shrimp for the price, making them difficult to share and they are large shrimp not jumbo, which makes the value poor. It would probably be better to either double up on the filet which was an excellent choice or perhaps grab another protein. We also decided to try the macaroni and cheese and grilled vegetables as a couple of additional sides. The description of the macaroni and cheese sounded delightful and we asked about it with our server he said it was truly incredible. I have a couple of very important suggestion I have regarding side items. First, skip the vegetables as they were just "okay" as a mixture of zucchini, green peppers and string beans, mostly. Next, I would advise that if you do get a side item such as the macaroni and cheese which was incredibly delightful it would be best for you to eat that first as the rest of your meal will wait. We decided to nibble on this along the way and unfortunately about halfway through our entrées we discovered that it got cold a little too quickly and didn't taste as nearly as good at room temperature as it did when it was hot. For dessert we decided on the "Dark and Dulce" and a couple of glasses of Grand Marnier. The dessert was described as "a classic flavor combination featuring our dark chocolate and sweet, thick dulce de leche accented with coarse ground sea salt". It was served with an assortment of side items on one, plate, even though you pay per person. Items included some bananas, strawberries, poundcake, rice crispy treats, blonde and chocolate brownies and dusted marshmallows. Other than the fruit, everything we tried seemed off. I'd swear that the rice crispy treats were actually stale. We ended up asking for additional strawberries and bananas and giving back the entire plate. We were brought out a couple of bowls of strawberries and bananas both of which were quite fresh and delicious. Overall this dessert tasted wonderful

text: This place is so bad it feels like a lost Chappelle Show skit--what would a wine shop be like if Deebo worked the register. I mean, I'm basically a socialist, and this place makes me extol the virtues of private enterprise. The selection is terrible, and the workers are uniformly rude, unprofessional, unhelpful, and just generally awful. I've been going to this and other West Philly PA Wine & Spirits stores for about five years now (this one hasn't been open that long), and in that time, not a single employee has ever greeted me or asked me if they could help me, let alone made a recommendation. And they work in a god damn service industry! To get a sense of just how much of a failure the PA Wine & Liquor system is, first go to this store, then walk about four blocks over to the privately owned (beer) Bottle Shop at Local 44. And the service at Local 44 isn't stellar, but compared to the wine & liquor store, it's like being waited on by fucking Spratt from Downton Abbey (incidentally, a Spratt/Deebo buddy flick is long overdue). What's maddening about the whole thing is that there's no reason it needs to be so terrible. You don't need an advanced degree to be friendly, polite, and knowledgeable about wine/liquor. You just need to have basic social skills and give a fuck about the industry you're working in (shit, with public libraries, you don't even need money or an internet connection to learn about wine). Apart from the appalling disservice these stores (and this store in particular) do to the PA public, they arguably do an even greater disservice to their employees. Because eventually (and I suspect sooner rather than later), there's going to be a referendum on privatizing these stores, and with all of their experience working in the wine/liquor business, these employees OUGHT to be first in line to open their own stores or be hired to help run a store. But the idea that a private wine shop would ever hire these employees is, unfortunately, laughable. And that's a huge fucking disservice to the employees, who will be left unemployed once privitization occurs, and all their 'experience' will count for nothing. If these stores can't make a very quick, very radical improvement in selection and service, they need to be done away with.

text: I recently bought my wedding gown from Country Way Bridal for my wedding in October. My experience seemed to be fine until my wedding gown came in. When I tried my gown on, It wasn't exactly how the sample was. The back lace was thicker, the straps were thicker and also shorter. I was very concerned however the owner Yvonne explained their seamstress is amazing and could fix anything. When I went back in for my first fitting, the seamstress who was extremely nice but quiet was pinning everything that she was going to fix. When I got home and saw the pictures, I immediately started the cry. I went from having too much lace in the back to nothing and I went from having a sweat heart shaped top to a V-neck. I immediately called the next day right when they opened and asked to speak to the owner Yvonne. I was told she was with a bride at the moment but should be able to call me back in about 30 minutes. After 2 1/2 hours, I called back and was told the owner had left. I explained that I was waiting for a phone call and needed to speak with her ASAP beings that they were closed the next day and I didn't want my gown to be touched. I wanted to send it back for a new one. I was then told she was at a family engagement and couldn't call me. I told them to let their owner know I was extremely upset with how unprofessional I thought it was that I did not get a call back. About 1 hour later, I had a missed call from a blocked number and it was the owner. She left me a 5 minute message (she actually got cut off because it was so long) and she was extremely nasty. She explained she was very upset with the way I spoke about her store and that they don't need to deal with that during a very busy trunk sale day. She went on to say I ruined her family engagement now and that she doesn't think it is good that we do business anymore if this is how I am going to act (after I had already paid in full). That night I e-mailed the designed Marisa personally and sent the before and after pictures to her. Thank goodness I did this because I do not believe I would have gotten a new dress if it wasn't for the designer. She was extremely professional and made a perfect dress for me within 3 months. When I went to pick up my new dress, the owner refused to even acknowledge me or ask me if I was happy with the new gown. The only words she said to me was, "Have a Nice Day" as I walked out the door. The girls working there were extremely professional and I feel bad they don't have a better role model to work under. I knew in that moment I wouldn't feel comfortable going back there for alterations nor did I trust them with my wedding gown. Today I finally took my gown out of their store and will be getting my alterations done somewhere else and a weight has been lifted from my shoulders. No bride to be should feel that way when trying on their wedding gown nor should they feel that kind of stress with everything they are already planning and dealing with. I will never set foot in this store every again and I will let every woman I work with know the hell I had to deal with from the owner Yvonne. On our second visit 2 weeks later, for lunch, we had just amazing French onion soup and the delightful galettes complet, which feature ham and eggs. These heavier crepes were great for lunch, and the soup warmed on a cold day. But honestly, the quiche Lorraine we also ordered was inedible, with much too much salt and nutmeg, perhaps indicating some chef error. There was so much nutmeg, I worried that if I ate the quiche, the little-known hallucinatory effects of the spice would make themselves known during the afternoon. I sent it back and they were gracious again, offering a free dessert crepe. We again had the hazelnut and caramel crepes which were just as we remembered, and a deliciously light and flavorful raspberry lemon crepe. All in all, I think that this place will do well, and fills a niche that otherwise goes empty in Indy. The food, atmosphere and service are all very nice, but I think that the team here needs a little more seasoning before they're ready for prime time.
